headings.title: Contractual capacity of qualified self-supporting minors
headings.reviewNote: Sets four conjunctive conditions for 16- or 17-year-old homeless or domestic-violence-victim minors who are self-supporting and have express or implied parental consent to contract for listed necessities and services.

headings.title: Capacity of minors in division custody to contract for auto insurance
headings.reviewNote: Covers qualification of minors aged 16 or older in children's division custody to contract for automobile insurance with court or division consent, and associated liability.

headings.title: Capacity of minors in division custody to open bank accounts
headings.reviewNote: Covers authorization of minors aged 16 or older in children's division custody to contract for bank accounts with consent, and associated liability for fees.

headings.title: Contracting entity immunity and bar on disaffirmance
headings.reviewNote: Grants civil and criminal immunity to entities and licensed providers contracting under subsection 1 except for gross negligence or willful or wanton acts or omissions, and bars age-based disaffirmance of consent.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text; revised subsection 1 title to reflect conjunctive eligibility requirements and subsection 4 title to remove unsupported "good-faith reliance" phrasing and include the disaffirmance bar.

headings.title: Definitions for relative caregiver consent
headings.reviewNote: Defines adult, child or minor, educational services, health care provider, parent, and relative caregiver for sections 431.058 to 431.062.

headings.title: Relative caregiver consent to medical treatment and educational services
headings.reviewNote: Covers authority of relative caregivers acting under affidavit to consent to medical treatment and educational services upon parental delegation or reasonable effort.

headings.title: Parental decisions supersede relative caregiver consent
headings.reviewNote: Covers parental authority to supersede relative caregiver decisions, provided parental decisions do not threaten the child's life, health, or safety.

headings.title: Immediate notice and invalidation when child leaves caregiver
headings.reviewNote: Covers obligation of relative caregiver to notify providers and schools immediately when the child stops living with caregiver, invalidating the affidavit.

headings.title: One-year expiration of relative caregiver affidavit
headings.reviewNote: Covers expiration of caregiver affidavit one year after submission or signing.

headings.title: Continued parental liability for medical and educational expenses
headings.reviewNote: Covers retention of parental liability for payment of medical treatment or educational services provided pursuant to relative caregiver consent.

headings.title: Caregiver immunity from liability upon statutory compliance
headings.reviewNote: Covers prohibition against creating causes of action against relative caregivers who comply with statutory provisions.

headings.title: Mandatory contents and execution of relative caregiver affidavit
headings.reviewNote: Covers required statutory elements and verification under penalty of perjury for relative caregiver affidavits.

headings.title: Statutory form for relative caregiver affidavit
headings.reviewNote: Covers permissible statutory form and content for relative caregiver affidavits.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 9 subsections (including statutory affidavit form) against archived text; noted catchline-vs-body mismatch (catchline cites immunization only while body covers section 431.061 medical treatment and educational services) and expanded subsection 1 reviewNote to list all six defined terms.

headings.title: Persons authorized to consent to surgical or medical treatment
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory list of persons authorized to consent to medical or surgical treatment, including adults, parents, certain minors, and relative caregivers.

headings.title: Liberal construction including adoptive and step-relationships
headings.reviewNote: Covers liberal statutory construction extending family relationships to adoptive, step, and half-blood relationships.

headings.title: Sufficiency of consent by single authorized person
headings.reviewNote: Covers rule that consent by one authorized person suffices notwithstanding protests or lack of consent from other authorized persons.

headings.title: Justified reliance on good-faith representations of authority
headings.reviewNote: Covers justified reliance by medical providers acting in good faith without contrary notice upon representations of identity, age, and authority.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text (including cross-references and 1985 Missouri Osteopathic Foundation case annotation): authorized medical/surgical consenters, liberal relationship construction, single-person consent sufficiency, and good-faith reliance.

headings.title: Priority order of consent for experimental treatment in teaching hospitals
headings.reviewNote: Covers order of priority among legal guardians, attorneys-in-fact, and family members to consent to experimental treatment in teaching hospitals for incapacitated adults.

headings.title: Prohibition against consent contrary to patient's expressed permission
headings.reviewNote: Covers prohibition against surrogate consent that contravenes the incapacitated adult's expressed wishes or permission.

headings.title: Life-threatening emergency exception and institutional review board waiver
headings.reviewNote: Covers emergency research exception dispensing with consent in life-threatening emergencies pursuant to institutional review board approval and federal regulations.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 3 subsections against archived text (effective 6-12-06): teaching-hospital surrogate consent priority for experimental treatment, bar against contravening expressed permission, and life-threatening emergency IRB waiver under federal regulations.

headings.title: Payment of life insurance proceeds up to ten thousand dollars to married minors
headings.reviewNote: Covers insurer authorization to pay life insurance proceeds up to ten thousand dollars directly to married minor beneficiaries without conservatorship.

headings.title: Signed acknowledgment as legal receipt
headings.reviewNote: Covers legal sufficiency of the married minor beneficiary's signed acknowledgment as a valid legal receipt for insurance proceeds.

headings.title: Prohibition against disaffirmance upon reaching age twenty-one
headings.reviewNote: Covers prohibition against disaffirmance of receipt or acknowledgment upon the minor attaining twenty-one years of age.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 3 subsections against archived text: permissive direct payment up to $10,000 of spousal life insurance proceeds to married minors aged 18 or older, legal receipt effect, and bar on disaffirmance at age 21.

headings.title: Voluntary blood donation by persons aged seventeen or older
headings.reviewNote: Covers authority of individuals aged seventeen or older to donate blood voluntarily without parental consent.

headings.title: Blood donation by sixteen-year-olds with written parental permission
headings.reviewNote: Covers authorization for sixteen-year-olds to donate blood upon obtaining written permission from a parent or guardian.

headings.title: Written authorization required for compensation of minor blood donors
headings.reviewNote: Covers prohibition against minors under eighteen receiving compensation for blood donations without written parental or guardian authorization.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 3 subsections against archived text: permissive voluntary blood donation at age 17+, 16-year-old donation with written parental/guardian permission, and written authorization required for minor compensation.

headings.title: Prompt payment duty under private design and construction contracts
headings.reviewNote: Covers duty of parties to private design or construction contracts entered after August 28, 1995, to make scheduled payments.

headings.title: Civil action, interest up to one and one-half percent, and attorney fees
headings.reviewNote: Covers civil actions for nonpayment, allowing discretionary interest up to one and one-half percent per month, attorney fees, and arbitration remedies.

headings.title: Exemption for owner-occupied residential property of four units or less
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory exemption of private construction contracts for owner-occupied residential properties of four units or less.

headings.title: Scope of private design and construction work
headings.reviewNote: Defines design or construction work to include building, roadway, structure, or real-property work, demolition or excavation, and related professional services; original-rolls footnote notes word "of" for "or".

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text including original-rolls footnote ("of" for "or" in subsection 4): private design/construction prompt payment, civil action with discretionary 1.5%/month interest and attorney fees or arbitration, four-unit owner-occupied exemption, and work scope.

headings.title: Payment schedule for property transportation contracts
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement to pay property transportation providers according to contract terms or within thirty days following timely, undamaged delivery.

headings.title: Civil action for failure to pay transportation providers
headings.reviewNote: Covers authorization for unpaid transportation providers to bring a civil action in a court of competent jurisdiction.

headings.title: Manufacturer reimbursement rates for equipment warranty repair work
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement that power equipment manufacturers reimburse retailers for warranty work at rates equal to or exceeding nonwarranty hourly labor rates.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 3 subsections against archived text: scheduled or 30-day payment for property transportation, civil action for nonpayment, and manufacturer warranty repair labor rate reimbursement under section 407.850.

headings.title: Enforceability of employee nonsolicitation and noninterference covenants
headings.reviewNote: Covers criteria for enforceable employee nonrecruitment and nonsolicitation covenants between business entities or employers and employees.

headings.title: Conclusive presumption of reasonableness for covenants up to one year
headings.reviewNote: Covers determination of reasonableness based on facts and circumstances, with conclusive presumption for employer covenants up to one year.

headings.title: Noncompetition covenants unaffected
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that subdivisions (3) and (4) of subsection 1 do not create or affect employer-employee noncompetition covenants; original-rolls footnote notes omitted word "this".

headings.title: Enforceability in other circumstances protecting legitimate business interests
headings.reviewNote: Covers enforceability of noninterference covenants in other circumstances where reasonably necessary to protect legally permissible business interests.

headings.title: Protection of employee right to seek and accept employment
headings.reviewNote: Preserves an employee's right to seek or accept employment with another employer upon or after voluntary or nonvoluntary termination (archived text reads "Nothing is this section").

headings.title: Retrospective and prospective effect
headings.reviewNote: Covers express legislative declaration that section 431.202 applies retrospectively as well as prospectively.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 6 subsections against archived text (effective 7-01-01), noting original-rolls footnote ("this" in subsection 3) and archived typographical error ("Nothing is this section" in subsection 5).

headings.title: Presumption of enforceability for owner nonrecruitment covenants up to two years
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a presumption of enforceability and non-restraint of trade under section 416.031(1) for written owner nonrecruitment covenants lasting up to two years after the business relationship ends.

headings.title: Presumption of enforceability for customer nonsolicitation covenants up to five years
headings.reviewNote: Covers presumption of enforceability for owner customer nonsolicitation covenants limited to dealt customers and lasting up to five years.

headings.title: Presumption of enforceability for advance notice of ownership transfer
headings.reviewNote: Covers presumption of enforceability for written provisions requiring business owners to give prior notice of intent to sell or dispose of ownership interests.

headings.title: Judicial modification and partial enforcement of overbroad covenants
headings.reviewNote: Covers mandatory judicial modification and partial enforcement of overbroad covenants to the extent reasonably necessary to protect business interests.

headings.title: Other covenants and confidentiality agreements unaffected
headings.reviewNote: Covers clarification that section 431.204 does not create or affect noncompetes, confidentiality agreements, or other covenants except as provided.

headings.title: Protection of owner right to seek and accept subsequent employment
headings.reviewNote: Covers reservation of owner's right to seek or accept employment with another entity following relationship termination, subject to notice covenants.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 6 subsections against archived text (L. 2023 S.B. 103); removed unstated "rebuttable" qualifier from subsection 1 reviewNote to stay strictly faithful to statutory text.
